issues.description: The Stock.findStockIngredient method signature is inconsistent between the problem specification/solution and the template. The problem UML (and the solution implementation) specify findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (single String parameter), but the template Stock.java defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with a caseSensitive parameter. Furthermore, within the template Stock.java the add and take methods call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, which does not match the defined two-parameter signature — creating an internal template contradiction that will prevent successful compilation and confuses students about the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Stock.java to provide the single-argument signature findStockIngredient(String) to match the problem statement and solution. Either change the existing method signature to findStockIngredient(String) or add an overload findStockIngredient(String) that delegates to the two-parameter version (e.g., defaulting caseSensitive to true). Also ensure internal calls in add/take use the matching single-argument method so the template compiles and aligns with the specified API.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock.findStockIngredient(String) method (single String parameter) to locate ingredients by name, but the template's Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (an extra boolean parameter). This divergence breaks the direct mapping from the exercise specification to the starter code (and causes callers in the template to not match the method signature), creating confusion and potential compilation errors for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template to the specification by providing a single-argument method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either change the template method signature to remove the boolean parameter or add an overload findStockIngredient(String) that delegates to the case-sensitive variant, so student code and the specification match the intended API.
